summary: Runciter returns from Switzerland and discovers that Miss Wirt, representing Stanton Mick, has approached him about decontaminating a secret project on Luna. Using his telepath Nina Freede, Runciter learns that Mick's project involves an experimental interstellar drive and that telepaths have infiltrated it. Runciter presents Pat to the firm, noting her danger symbols but agreeing to hire her. He assembles a group of eleven inertials to deploy against the PSIs, and then the narrative fractures: Pat demonstrates her power by altering reality. Joe suddenly finds himself looking at a shop window in New York, having forgotten what he's supposed to be doing. When he refocuses, he discovers time has been changed—he and Pat are now married, and Stanton Mick may not have become Runciter's client. The chapter collapses into reality distortion.

locations.context: Runciter's personal executive office with massive walnut-and-leather furniture

locations.name: Map room
locations.context: Strategic center displaying locations of inertials and PSIs; visual representation of the hidden conflict

locations.name: Luna
locations.context: The Moon; location of Techprise research facility being infiltrated by telepaths

locations.name: Fifth Avenue, New York
locations.context: Where Runciter momentarily experiences an alternate reality, studying rare coins in a shop window

characters.name: Glen Runciter
characters.role_in_chapter: Protagonist managing crisis and assembling team; increasingly overtaken by reality shifts
characters.key_actions: Speaks with Tamish about ad strategy; meets with Miss Wirt; learns about Luna project; assembles inertial team; experiences brief alternate reality; reassembles after reset

characters.name: Miss Wirt
characters.role_in_chapter: Stanton Mick's confidential assistant; represents hidden power structure
characters.key_actions: Requests fast anti-PSI deployment; refuses to name employer initially; carries enormous financial authority; negotiates contract

characters.name: Stanton Mick
characters.role_in_chapter: Wealthy industrialist and speculator; never appears directly; represented through Miss Wirt
characters.key_actions: Initiates contact with Runciter Associates; proposes mass colonization via advanced drive; represented as Runciter's new biggest client

characters.name: Pat Conley
characters.role_in_chapter: The newly hired anti-talent whose power manifests catastrophically
characters.key_actions: Demonstrates her ability by changing reality during the assembly; transforms her relationship with Joe; displays mastery over business outcomes

characters.name: Nina Freede
characters.role_in_chapter: Runciter's resident telepath; reads Miss Wirt's mind
characters.key_actions: Provides intelligence on Mick and the Luna project; enables Runciter's strategic decisions

characters.name: Tamish
characters.key_actions: Discusses advertising strategy; reminds Runciter about business context

characters.name: Joe Chip
characters.role_in_chapter: Tester and now husband of Pat in altered timeline
characters.key_actions: Tests Pat; marries Pat (in altered timeline); becomes increasingly aware of reality shifts

themes: Corporate power and hidden ownership structures
The manipulation of reality by superior technologies/abilities
Marriage and intimate entanglement as forms of control
Advertising and narrative control of public perception
The fragility of shared consensus reality
Employment as a mechanism of social organization

theological_concepts.context: Pat's ability to alter the past suggests godlike knowledge and control over all moments simultaneously
theological_concepts.theological_frame: Boethian theology of God's eternal present; Calvinist predestination

theological_concepts.concept: The nature of memory as spiritual essence
theological_concepts.context: When Pat changes the past, only Joe retains vestigial memory—suggesting consciousness as the seat of persistence
theological_concepts.theological_frame: Platonic anamnesis (remembrance); Augustine's theology of memory and identity

philosophical_concepts.concept: Metaphysics of identity: Joe remains 'Joe' even when married to Pat in the altered timeline; what maintains identity across timeline shifts?
The nature of contracts and agreement: Do agreements made in one timeline bind behavior in another?
Epistemological privilege: Joe has knowledge of multiple timelines; does this constitute a form of enlightenment or curse?
Political economy: The negotiation between Runciter and Mick represents power plays between industrial entities
Feminist philosophy: Pat's power emerges from outside the male corporate structure and disrupts its logic entirely

key_events.event: Miss Wirt approaches Runciter with the Luna project
key_events.significance: Introduces the hidden plot that will drive later action; reveals that Hollis's missing PSIs may be employed by Mick

key_events.event: Runciter assembles the group of eleven inertials
key_events.significance: Creates the team that will form the narrative's traveling party; represents the culmination of pre-crisis planning

key_events.event: Pat alters reality during the assembly meeting
key_events.significance: The novel's central mystery erupts into narrative; marks the point where reality becomes unreliable to readers and characters alike

key_events.event: Joe discovers his marriage to Pat in the altered timeline
key_events.significance: Establishes Pat's power over personal relationships and memories; entangles the entire team with her modifications
